lesson-intro.text: A bicycle is two circles and a handful of straight lines. There's hardly any coloring, so every line counts. Watch how the lines meet at the corners, then ride along.

back-wheel.text: The back wheel is a big circle. Draw one half, then the other.

front-wheel.text: The front wheel matches it. Leave room between them for the frame.

hubs.text: Mark the center of each wheel with a tiny circle.

seat-tube.text: The frame begins with one slanted line, from under the seat down to where the pedals go.

back-triangle.text: From the back hub, draw one line to the top of that tube and one to the bottom.

main-triangle.text: Next, a level bar forward from the seat, and a slanted bar up from the pedals to meet it.

fork.text: The fork holds the front wheel. From above the bars, come down through the corner to the front hub.

handlebars.text: Lay the handlebars flat across the top, like the top of a T.

saddle.text: The seat is a small wedge, round at the back and pointed at the front.

lesson-outro.text: Two circles and nine lines, and it really is a bicycle. Lean it somewhere safe.
